howTo.title: How to Create a Photography Invoice
howTo.subtitle: Professional invoices for photo sessions, licensing, and print delivery in three simple steps.

steps.title: Add Studio Branding and Shoot Information
steps.description: Enter your photography business name, studio logo, contact email, client name, and event or shoot location.
steps.tip: Adding your visual studio logo creates immediate trust with commercial and wedding clients.

steps.title: Itemize Session Time, Edits, and Usage Rights
steps.description: Break down coverage hours, second-shooter fees, retouching time, and commercial licensing rights.
steps.tip: Clearly separate creative labor fees from commercial image licensing rights.

steps.title: Download the PDF or Export a PNG
steps.description: Choose from four clean templates and export an unwatermarked vector PDF or high-resolution PNG image.
steps.tip: State your booking retainer policy clearly (such as a 50% non-refundable booking deposit).

whatItMustContain.title: What a Photography Invoice Must Contain
whatItMustContain.subtitle: Essential items every professional photographer must document to protect creative rights and avoid disputes.
whatItMustContain.disclaimer: General information, not legal or tax advice. Check your local rules.

items.title: Studio Identity and Contact Details
items.description: Your registered photography business name, studio address, tax ID, and contact phone number.

items.title: Shoot Date, Duration, and Venue
items.description: The exact calendar date, hours of coverage, and physical shoot venue or studio address.

items.title: Itemized Creative Services
items.description: Session hours, assistant photographer fees, lighting gear rentals, and post-production color grading.

items.title: Image Usage Rights and Licensing
items.description: Specific declaration of personal vs commercial usage, media territory (for example, North America or Worldwide), and license duration (such as 1 Year or Perpetual).

items.title: Deliverables and File Formats
items.description: Number of edited high-resolution digital images, gallery delivery method, and included print dimensions.

items.title: Payment Schedule and Retainer Policy
items.description: Non-refundable booking retainer amount and due date for the remaining balance before gallery handover [Verify with official source: state sales tax rules on digital photography deliverables vs tangible prints].

faq.title: Photography Invoicing FAQs
faq.subtitle: Frequently asked questions regarding photo retainers, licensing fees, and print taxes.

items.question: When should wedding and portrait photographers collect payment?
items.answer: Standard industry practice is collecting a 30% to 50% non-refundable booking deposit to reserve the calendar date, with the remaining balance due 14 to 30 days before the event or prior to final image delivery.

items.question: How do I specify photo usage rights on an invoice?
items.answer: Add a dedicated line item or note defining the exact scope: media type (Web, Social Media, Print, Broadcast), geographic region (Local, National, Worldwide), and duration (1 Year, Perpetual).

items.question: Should sales tax be charged on photography services?
items.answer: Tax regulations vary by jurisdiction. In many US states, digital-only image delivery is non-taxable, while delivering tangible prints or flash drives makes the entire transaction subject to sales tax [Verify with official source: state sales tax department on photography].

items.question: Can I export an image version of my invoice for clients on messaging apps?
items.answer: Yes. In addition to high-resolution vector PDF downloads, you can click 'Export PNG' to save a clean image ready to text or send via WhatsApp.
